feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, video, and budget.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete scope: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership through a blend of strategy, platform delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes recur almost verbatim, which weakens impact.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lift, production savings, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or operational efficiencies.  
- Tighten style consistency: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other compounds, and list punctuation around phrases like “web, email, social, and multimedia.” No major misspellings found; grammar is strong overall. Minor stylistic issue: “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and reads promotional rather than candidate-focused.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas already covered elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the list of focus areas to the most distinctive themes: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Consider rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Delivers scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled discovery experiences that improve how mission-driven institutions publish, measure, and serve users.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “multimedia production” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Recent Projects; “AI-enabled discovery experiences” is more specific.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made slightly more distinctive, and aligned in style.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Replace vague or repetitive items with sharper terms tied to recent work: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”
- Clarify operational scope: “Workflow automation and platform integrations” and “Multimedia production, studio, and livestream operations”
- Consider a more concise final version: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia, studio, and livestream operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well covered elsewhere, so keep it only if targeting roles where sector context is essential.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce your recent work, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding light outcome/context cues will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add bullets or line breaks under “Recent Projects” so each item scans quickly; keep each project to one crisp sentence.
- Use parallel action/result structure: “Built/Developed/Launched X to achieve Y.”
- Tighten wording and reduce stacked nouns: e.g., “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Consider this rewrite:  
  **AI Hybrid Search** — Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite** — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources in a modular framework designed to scale.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign** — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display.  
  **Advocacy Video Series** — Produced a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsite development, and advocacy video work are already reflected in recent roles; keep this block project-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary with “Led,” “Produced,” or “Launched.”

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten the scope, foreground leadership/ownership, and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, with ownership across Drupal, analytics, governance, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with stronger ones: lead, architect, streamline, modernize, launch, optimize.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-focused lines, e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics and governance/usability/operations.
- Add measurable context where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign outputs launched, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, engagement or conversion gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with the footer project list; avoid repeating specific microsites/campaigns here unless you add outcomes not mentioned there.
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “Drupal” already appear heavily in prior NACo roles, so emphasize what is new: freelance ownership, AI search, enterprise workflow redesign, or cross-channel modernization.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational scope, and the most senior-level achievements without repeating duties covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine platform and migration detail into one impact bullet: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channels/results more outcome-focused: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with metrics on growth, engagement, or deliverability if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting…” / “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video operations overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- “Advocacy programming” and recurring video content also appear in Recent Projects/footer.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as responsibilities than outcomes. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and the systems/editorial improvements that set up the later director role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to show progression and impact: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing during a period of organizational growth.”
- Combine newsletter work into one sharper bullet: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, improving cadence and consistency across core member communications.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-led: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel across web, email and social.”
- Clarify systems/process value: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and publishing consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; differentiate this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format.
- “Publishing workflows/governance” overlaps with the 2022–2024 director role; keep this version tactical, not enterprise-level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior, recent leadership scope rather than repeating generic communications phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered campaign and advocacy content strategy
- Drop “messaging” and “content planning” as standalone phrases; they read broad and lower-impact than “content operations,” “governance,” or “campaign strategy.”
- If space allows, align language to recent roles by foregrounding enterprise platforms and governance over older editorial/generalist work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Core Competencies; consider using “cross-channel campaign strategy” to differentiate.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal-led modernization, integrations/automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, higher-level line: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are target-role keywords; they’re better left in Technical + IT.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to echo recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed platform/tool lists in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating it elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.:
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity
- Analytics infrastructure and dashboard development
- KPI framework design and executive reporting
- SEO, user behavior and performance optimization
- Put the most strategic items first: “KPI framework design” and “executive reporting” are stronger differentiators than listing platforms alone.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Board/executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- If accurate, consider adding one stronger outcome-oriented phrase such as “decision-ready dashboards” or “measurement strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; keep this section more strategic and the Technical section more platform-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery environment and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: “Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production”
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal bullets:
- Broadcast-quality studio production and operations
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production systems
- Video editing and post-production workflows
- If accurate, strengthen one bullet with scale/context: “Hybrid event production for advocacy, conference and member-facing programs”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video production and editing” is already implied by NACo studio/video achievements and the Technical + IT tools list.
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies wording; use “livestream and hybrid event delivery” to differentiate.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize recent/high-impact tools first: Drupal should clearly lead given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Consider dropping lower-signal items unless they support target roles; a tighter version could be: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages
- If you want stronger impact, add level/context instead of just names, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites and governance).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus modernization context.
- GitHub Pages may undersell seniority unless it is directly relevant to the roles you’re targeting.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Replace with a tighter list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value.
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier in parentheses, e.g., “API integrations (CMS, analytics, automation)” or “Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting/performance)” to show application, not just tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; consider removing them there or keeping this section as the detailed version.
- If GitHub Actions is only lightly used, cut it to avoid overstating depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance/strength: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”  
- Remove lower-value/older items unless actively used recently: Basecamp, Trello
- If space allows, add light functional context instead of a pure list: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams (workflow design, task orchestration, cross-team coordination)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating all three in the same wording.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar category signals; listing all four can look padded.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth rather than repeat channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier in the title or nearby skills grouping, e.g. “enterprise email, newsletter and member engagement platforms”
- Keep this as a platform list only; save outcomes like audience size, newsletter volume, or campaign impact for the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience bullets

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so don’t add broad channel language to this item unless it is specifically email/engagement-focused

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and reads as a generic keyword dump. Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization methods and keep the strongest platform names only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Replace with: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Swap “Dashboarding” for “KPI reporting” or “performance reporting” since it’s more outcome-oriented and less vague.
- If truthful, consider adding one higher-value capability over a generic term: “conversion analysis,” “funnel analysis,” or “tagging/measurement strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this section tools-only while the Topline section stays capability-focused.
- SEO is already implied elsewhere; “Google Search Console” is more concrete and less repetitive than “SEO.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or improvement in turnaround/production capacity.
- Tighten the leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and mentored a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the format, not scaling it.
- Avoid repeating general workflow language already used in later NACo entries unless you can add a distinct early-stage outcome.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes/ownership so it reads as a foundation for the later digital leadership roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research projects supporting NACo programs and policy initiatives.”
- Make the podcast achievement the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, or types of projects/campaigns supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “multimedia production” language already covered in later NACo roles; keep this focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here, since stronger team/strategy ownership appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
